stated: Reform UK will immediately deport foreign nationals after their prison sentence ends and withdraw citizenship from immigrants who commit crimes, with exceptions for minor misdemeanours.

source.quote: Immediate Deportation for Foreign Criminals Deport foreign nationals immediately after their prison sentence ends. Withdraw citizenship from immigrants who commit crime with the exception of some misdemeanour offences.

bearing_set.reason: Immediate post-sentence deportation of foreign nationals directly affects reoffending rates and public safety outcomes, earning a real verdict on crime and the justice system.

Withdrawing citizenship from immigrants who commit crimes raises concrete due-process, equal-treatment (differential treatment of naturalised vs. birth citizens), and statelessness/ECHR legal-rights issues — squarely within O9's strict scope.

Citizenship withdrawal and enforced removal from the country constitute significant state coercive powers over individuals' fundamental legal status and freedom of residence — concrete worsening of the 'freedom from state coercion' indicator, independent of the O9 due-process dimension.

membership_note: Three genuine bearings: O5 (safety benefit via elimination of domestic reoffending by deported individuals), O9 (equal-treatment and due-process cost of citizenship withdrawal and differential post-sentence consequences by immigration status), O10 (liberty cost of citizenship removal as a coercive state power beyond the judicially imposed sentence). No non-negligible fiscal (O12), labour (O4), or cohesion (O15) effects can be pinned to a specific indicator without speculative assumptions.
